record.paper_title: Completeness of sets of complex exponentials in convex sets: open problems
record.original_question: Let Λ = {λ_n} be a sequence of pairwise distinct complex numbers with 0 not in Λ and λ_n tending to infinity, and let Exp Λ = {exp(λ_n z)}. Let G be an unbounded convex domain in the complex plane containing [0,+∞), let Clos G be its closure, and define the width d_G by d_G = lim_{x→+∞} d_G(x), where d_G(x) is the supremum of |z−z′| over z,z′ ∈ G with Re z = Re z′ = x. For the remaining finite-width situations in which the available test for completeness of Exp Λ in H(Clos G) applies only when Λ is separated from the imaginary axis, what precise condition characterizes exactly when Exp Λ is complete in H(Clos G) without imposing that separation hypothesis?

evidence.quote: Let Λ = {λ_n}, n ∈ N, be a sequence of pairwise different complex numbers (points) in the complex plane C, 0 ∉ Λ, and λ_n → ∞ as n → +∞. Let X be a convex open or closed set on C. By H(X) denote the space of all continuous complex-valued functions on X which are holomorpic in the interior Int X of X (if Int X ≠ ∅) with the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets of X. An exponential system Exp Λ = {exp(λ_n z)} is complete in X if the closure of the linear span of Exp Λ in H(X) coincides with H(X).
4) X = Clos G, where G is the same as above, Clos G is the closure of G.
(4-?) The width of an unbounded convex domain G, [0,+∞) ⊂ G, is defined to be the quantity d_G = lim_{x→+∞} d_G(x), where d_G(x) = sup{|z−z′| : z,z′ ∈ G; Re z = Re z′ = x}, x ∈ [0,+∞).
In the opposite case, there is a test for the completeness of a system Exp Λ in Clos G only under conditions that the sequence Λ is separated from the imaginary axis.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let H(X) denote the space of complex-valued functions that are continuous on a convex set X ⊂ ℂ and holomorphic in its interior (when nonempty), equipped with the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets of X. For a sequence Λ = {λ_n}_{n∈ℕ} of pairwise distinct complex numbers with 0 ∉ Λ and λ_n → ∞, define the exponential system Exp Λ = {exp(λ_n z) : n ∈ ℕ}. We say Exp Λ is complete in H(X) if the closure of its linear span equals H(X).

Let G ⊂ ℂ be an unbounded convex domain containing the ray [0, +∞), and let Clos G denote its closure. For x ∈ [0, +∞) set
   d_G(x) = sup{ |z − z′| : z, z′ ∈ G, Re z = Re z′ = x },
and define the width of G by
   d_G = lim_{x → +∞} d_G(x),
assuming this limit is finite (the finite-width case).

Find a necessary and sufficient condition on Λ — not assuming that Λ is separated from the imaginary axis (i.e., not assuming inf_n |Re λ_n| > 0) — characterizing exactly when Exp Λ is complete in H(Clos G).
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature (e.g., works on completeness of exponential systems in geometric terms of width, breadth, and diameter, 2022–2023) provides completeness criteria for convex domains under additional separation or density hypotheses, but a complete characterization in the finite-width unbounded-convex-domain setting without assuming Λ is separated from the imaginary axis does not appear to be established. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Completeness of the exponential system in geometric terms of width, breadth and diameter
status_evidence.snippet: A criterion for the completeness of an exponential system has been established in spaces of holomorphic functions on convex domains in terms of breadth/width and logarithmic block densities of exponents.
status_evidence.claim: Recent criteria express completeness via width/breadth and density, but the finite-width case without the separation-from-imaginary-axis hypothesis is not fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: On complete and incomplete exponential systems
status_evidence.snippet: Tests for completeness in closures of unbounded convex domains typically require Λ separated from the imaginary axis.
status_evidence.claim: Available tests in the finite-width unbounded case still impose the separation hypothesis.
